study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Rehák Bučková et al., eLife Reviewed Preprint, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Using normative models pre-trained on cross-sectional data to evaluate intra-individual longitudinal changes in neuroimaging data

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the objective to adapt existing cross-sectional normative models for evaluating intra-individual longitudinal changes, introduce the z-diff metric, and illustrate the approach on a schizophrenia cohort. This satisfies both criteria: hypotheses/questions and purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We extend this framework to evaluate an individual's longitudinal change... introduce a quantitative metric termed 'zdiff'... (lines 42–48). We present a comprehensive theoretical analysis... and a practical application to an in-house longitudinal dataset... (line 70).

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses an existing pre-trained normative model (citing Rutherford et al. and Fraza et al.), and performs local adaptation using a healthy control sample. Eligibility criteria for local controls are described (age ≥18, no personal psychiatric disorder, no family history of psychosis; MRI contraindications excluded). Image quality standards are specified via Euler number QC with outliers excluded. Final sample sizes are reported (67 controls) after QC, and exclusion via QC is stated.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Original models were fit on 58,836 participants across 82 sites... validated... (line 115). Adaptation procedure... a sample of a reference (healthy) cohort measured on the same scanner... (line 119). Healthy controls over 18 years of age... no personal history... no family history... (lines 252–256). If a subject... any MRI contraindications, they were excluded (line 257). ...all subjects having a rescaled Euler number greater than ten were labelled outliers and were not included (lines 273–276). We analysed data from 98 patients... and 67 controls (line 244).

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The normative model includes covariates age and sex, and explicitly handles multi-site effects by appending site dummies to the basis expansion. Local site adaptation is also described.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: This framework models each IDP... as a function of... age, sex, scanning site (line 58). ...use a B-spline basis... To accommodate site-level effects, we append it with site dummies (line 87). ...evaluate subjects measured at a new site... run an adaptation procedure to account for its effect (line 119).

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source for the reference cohort is the pre-trained brain charts normative models trained on 58,836 participants across 82 sites. The paper cites the original publications and provides the GitHub repository for the estimates.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Original models were fit on a large dataset consisting of 58,836 participants scanned across 82 sites (line 115). ...the estimates are available at https://github.com/predictive-clinical-neuroscience/braincharts (line 153).

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: The study uses an existing normative model for the reference cohort; per guidance, acquisition protocol for secondary/existing datasets is not applicable.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing steps are described, including software and version (FreeSurfer v7.2 recon-all), use of both longitudinal and cross-sectional pipelines, and QC via rescaled Euler number thresholding.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: Prior to normative modelling, all T1 images were preprocessed using the Freesurfer v.(7.2) reconall pipeline... we additionally performed cross-sectional preprocessing (line 265). ...all subjects having a rescaled Euler number greater than ten were labelled outliers and were not included (lines 273–276).

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: An existing pre-trained normative model is used; per guidance, internal validation of a newly built reference model is not applicable.

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: An existing pre-trained normative model is used; per guidance, external validation of a newly built reference model is not applicable.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The study applies an existing normative model rather than developing a new one; per guidance this item is not applicable.

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses an existing reference model; performance metrics for the reference cohort are not newly reported here.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No new data partitioning for model development was performed; an existing model was used.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Reproducibility is supported by citing the source of the normative model (braincharts), naming the specific pre-trained model (lifespan_58K_82_sites), and providing software/tooling and tutorial links (PCNtoolkit). Software version for preprocessing (FreeSurfer v7.2) is also specified.

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Clinical covariates are incorporated by relating z-diff scores to longitudinal changes in clinical scales (PANSS and GAF). Additionally, the ANCOVA includes baseline thickness and demographics as covariates in conventional analyses.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: ...link the z-diff to the longitudinal changes in clinical scales (line 271). ...using Spearman correlation related the scores with changes in the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) and Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF) (line 298). The ANCOVA model... accounting for age, gender, and thickness in visit 1 (lines 290–294).

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: ...related the scores with changes in the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) and Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF) (line 298). Table 1 lists PANSS and GAF at both visits (lines 306–313).

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The z-diff score is defined and its interpretation as a standard normal deviation for healthy controls is explained, with group-level tests against zero and associations with clinical changes. However, explicit categorical thresholds for defining 'extreme' individuals in the clinical application are not specified (thresholds are discussed in simulation).
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: ...design a score... z-diff... to assess temporal changes... detect unusually pronounced deviations (line 125). Since this z-diff score is standard normal for the population of healthy controls, any large deviations may be used to detect unusual temporal changes (line 161). At a group-level, we identified regions with z-diff scores significantly different from zero... (lines 273–274). We imagine a practitioner... use the quantiles of the standard normal distribution as the thresholds... (lines 207–214).
